cases.title: Ethylene production: process design, techno-economic and life-cycle assessments
notes: Residence time is inferred from the reported 15.1 mol% residual ethane at the reactor outlet. Ethylene, hydrogen, methane, fresh ethane, heat, and compressor work remain test quantities.
The process description calls the reactor pressure ambient while Table 1 lists 4.5 bar. Both pressures are evaluated and the result is reported as a source-defined envelope.
The reported 3:1 ethane:steam volume ratio gives the reactor dilution input after molecular-weight conversion.
MSP and annual manufacturing cost are shown as economic context because the paper uses a 20-year discounted cash-flow MSP calculation.

cases.title: Decarbonization approaches for ethylene production: comparative techno-economic and life-cycle analysis
notes: The paper reports steam ratio and plant inventory but no single reactor temperature/residence-time/pressure triplet in the main article.
Residence time is fitted to fresh-ethane demand across 800–900 °C and 1–5 bar. C3+ production, total combustion heat, and on-site GHG remain test quantities.
The 17.2 GJ/t combustion-energy value is the paper's model-validation quantity and includes heat from imported natural gas plus hydrogen/methane purge gas.

cases.title: Development of a novel microwave-assisted process that converts waste polyethylene plastic to ethylene
notes: Residence time is derived from the published tube geometry and reactor-feed flow using ideal-gas volumetric flow at the arithmetic-mean reactor temperature and pressure; inlet and outlet states define a bracket.
The heating-ramp exponent is inferred from the published single-pass ethane conversion. Fresh ethane, recycle ethane, ethylene, CH4, H2, C3 and C4+ outlet fractions remain test quantities.

The web surrogate uses a 650 °C reactor inlet and pure ethane plus steam at the kinetic-model inlet. This paper reports 502.77 °C and 0.64 wt% ethylene in the reactor feed; those two differences remain explicit in the benchmark.
